methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $22M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
RISE Robotics is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Arron Acosta and Blake Sessions, having raised $22M+ to date. The valuation analysis triangulates against a comp universe of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public comparable, spanning seed through Series B stages.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $22M total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, implies a $44M valuation. Peer-median analysis references three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B (Series B), Dexterity at $1.6B (Series B), and Walden Robotics at $1.1B (Seed). The median of these three firms is $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $1.8B.

The triangulated analysis across both methods produces a range of $37M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $847M. The extreme disparity between stage-progression and peer-median methods reflects a material tension: the stage-progression method is constrained by capital deployed, while peer comparables span a wider stage distribution and exhibit substantially higher absolute valuations. Key uncertainties include RISE's relative product maturity versus the Series B peers, unit economics relative to comparables, and whether the $1.1B–$1.8B peer range is appropriately calibrated to a Series A entry point. A narrower range would require clarity on RISE's revenue trajectory and capital efficiency relative to the peer set.
